An e-bike rider is clinging to life after he was struck by a hit-and-run driver on a busy Brooklyn street Tuesday night, cops said.

The 33-year-old biker was riding south in the right lane on Nostrand Avenue near Atlantic Avenue in Crown Heights – a buzzing commercial intersection – around 7:30 p.m. when he was struck by the driver of a white 2026 Hyundai Elantra, police said.

The Elantra driver had been in the center lane before beginning to merge into the right lane, where the crash happened, authorities said.

The cyclist was thrown from the bike onto the pavement and suffered head trauma, according to cops.

He was rushed to the Kings County Hospital Center, where he remained in critical condition Wednesday, police said.

The Hyundai driver fled the scene, heading south on Nostrand Avenue, and remained on the lam, police said.

The crash comes weeks after a man riding an e-bike was fatally struck by a pick-up truck driver in the Bronx, cops and sources said.

The 50-year-old biker was heading west on East 145th Street when the truck driver, traveling south on Brook Avenue in Mott Haven, hit him around 8:25 a.m. Oct. 7, according to authorities and law enforcement sources.

The pick-up truck driver, a 55-year-old man, stayed at the scene and did not face any charges, police said.

And last month, a delivery woman was killed when a dump truck plowed into her e-bike and then drove off in the heart of Herald Square, according to cops and an advocacy group.

The truck driver collided with the 50-year-old cyclist the morning of Sept. 28, as both headed west on West 34th Street, approaching Seventh Avenue, police said.

The woman — who was riding a JOCO rental e-bike and making a delivery — was pronounced dead at the scene.

A compassionate Marine is still running a Long Island holiday toy drive for needy kids after three decades — even as he contends with the after-effects of a debilitating stroke.

Chuck Kilbride, a retired USMC Major and Long Island native who has led Nassau County’s Toys For Tots since the 1990s, showed up to help hand out toys to children from Hempstead at Miller’s Ale House in Levittown despite his health issues on Wednesday.

Kilbride, 73, suffered a stroke last October that left him struggling with aphasia — a debilitating brain disorder that impairs the ability to speak, understand, read and write — but the vet hasn’t let it slow him down.

“Altogether, it’s probably been over 2 million [toys],” Kilbride said of the number of trinkets he’s given out to children in his more than 30-year career.

He was honored on Wednesday during the drive by county government officials who said his decades of commitment and refusal to step back makes him a role model.

“He [just] wants to make sure all these kids are happy for the holiday season,” Toys For Tots co-chairmen Sean Acosta, who helped lead the honors for Kilbride, told The Post.

“He wants to make sure he puts a smile on every one of these kids’ faces — he collects the toys — [but] he never takes recognition, and that’s why this year we’re recognizing him,” Acosta said.

Kilbride first enlisted in 1971 and served 27 years in the Marines. He took on the responsibility of running the massive toy drive almost immediately after retiring, eventually earning a spot in the New York State Veterans Hall of Fame.

He has since spent the next three decades rallying donors, volunteers and local officials behind the cause.

After his stroke last year, some thought he would begin to take a step back from his duties — but instead, he kept pushing forward for the children that serve as his inspiration.

“He is relentless, determined. He doesn’t quit,” his daughter, retired Army Captain Kate Hiebert, 52, told The Post.

“Toys for Tots became a mechanism for him to coordinate the generosity of everyone else to give to the next generation of kids, and I think also to teach them that there are people who care, and that this is the way you can give,” she said.

But the humble vet was quick to pass the credit to the officials and workers he’s teamed up with for years as they sung his praises and passed the credit right back to him.

“That’s the Marines,” Acosta said. “He keeps going no matter what.”
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. یک تفنگدار دلسوز هنوز هم پس از سه دهه یک اسباب‌بازی در تعطیلات لانگ آیلند برای بچه‌های نیازمند راه‌اندازی می‌کند - حتی در شرایطی که با اثرات بعدی یک سکته مغزی ناتوان کننده دست و پنجه نرم می‌کند. چاک کیلبراید، سرگرد بازنشسته USMC و بومی لانگ آیلند که از دهه 1990 هدایت اسباب‌بازی‌های کودکان ناسائو کانتی را بر عهده داشت، در روز چهارشنبه با وجود مشکلات سلامتی، برای کمک به توزیع اسباب‌بازی‌ها به بچه‌های همپستد در خانه میلرز آل در لویت‌تاون حضور یافت. کیلبرید، 73 ساله، اکتبر گذشته دچار سکته مغزی شد که باعث شد او با آفازی دست و پنجه نرم کند - یک اختلال مغزی ناتوان کننده که توانایی صحبت کردن، درک کردن، خواندن و نوشتن را مختل می کند - اما دامپزشک اجازه نداده است که سرعت او را کاهش دهد. حرفه او روز چهارشنبه در جریان رانندگی توسط مقامات دولتی کانتی مورد تجلیل قرار گرفت و گفتند که چندین دهه تعهد و امتناع او از عقب‌نشینی او را به یک الگو تبدیل می‌کند. شان آکوستا، یکی از روسای Toys For Tots، که به رهبری افتخارات Kilbride کمک کرد، به The Post گفت: «او [فقط] می‌خواهد مطمئن شود که همه این بچه‌ها برای فصل تعطیلات خوشحال هستند. آکوستا گفت: «او می‌خواهد مطمئن شود که روی صورت هر یک از این بچه‌ها لبخند می‌زند - او اسباب‌بازی‌ها را جمع‌آوری می‌کند - [اما] او هرگز به رسمیت شناخته نمی‌شود، و به همین دلیل است که امسال ما او را می‌شناسیم.» کیلبرید برای اولین بار در سال 1971 به خدمت گرفت و 27 سال در تفنگداران دریایی خدمت کرد. او مسئولیت runnin را بر عهده گرفت

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Natisha “Tish” Long is familiar with what’s considered to be the most agonizing sensations known to humans.

Since 2018, an unbearable “shocking, throbbing pain” would course through her face at random, lasting from seconds to minutes each time.

“When I got my shocks, it was all-in-one, everything hit me,” she told The Post. Every second that passed felt like an eternity. “It’s just there and you’re waiting for it to ease up. Sometimes I’d have to stop and just wait until that whole shock was over with before I could function.”

The mom of four has trigeminal neuralgia, a neurological condition nicknamed the “suicide disease” because of how brutal its episodes are.

“You can’t smile, you can’t brush your teeth, you can’t wash your face. Any little thing, the wind hitting it, it’s pain,” Long said.

It’s no surprise that these episodes cause extreme emotional distress, anxiety and depression. It’s not just a nickname — research shows people with this disease are at increased risk of suicide and self harm.

But experts are trying to move away from the nickname because treatment options are available that provide long-term relief. After seven long years, Long found it for herself with a first-in-the-world procedure at University Hospitals in Ohio.

“It was very, very hard to function because I still had to work and be a mom,” she said. “I was working through pain … I don’t know how I did it. When I look back, I’m like, how did I go to work for 12 hours and put like this little game face on?”

Her condition stole both her signature smile and bubbly personality.

“At work, people could see [the pain] in my face,” she said. They’d ask her what’s wrong, and in response, “I had to mumble. I couldn’t really open my mouth too much so I wouldn’t get triggered; I tried to be as quiet as possible.”

“You’re going to sleep in pain, you’re waking up in the pain. [My friends] always knew, Tish has to have her bag of pills.”

It all started with tingling on her upper jaw. She saw a dentist multiple times, who couldn’t find anything wrong. She was prescribed a new toothpaste and mouthwash, but neither helped.

The pain spread down to her lower jaw and got worse. She saw a physician, who suggested it might be facial neuropathy, a broader category of nerve dysfunction in the face that can include numbness and constant, dull pain.

Doctors prescribed gabapentin and carbamazepine, which initially helped.

“As soon as you wake up, you take your pills because you’re gonna wake up in pain,” she said. “You’re going to sleep in pain, you’re waking up in the pain. [My friends] always knew, Tish has to have her bag of pills … if I forgot, I’m like, I got to go home. You know, I can’t function.”

But soon, her episodes became even more frequent and intense, breaking through the little relief the medicine provided.

The most common form of the condition occurs when a blood vessel presses against the trigeminal nerve near the brainstem. The pressure can damage the nerve’s protective covering, causing it to send pain signals erratically.

This causes that “shocking, shooting, stabbing, lancing pain in your face,” explains neurosurgeon Dr. Michael Staudt, who treated Long at University Hospitals.

Those medications Long was taking were originally developed to treat seizures, but they can also help calm overactive nerves and relieve nerve pain. Patients often have to increase their dose rapidly to keep up with worsening episodes, making tradeoffs with side effects like brain fog, confusion, and weight gain, Staudt said.

Still, medication “doesn’t work for everybody,” he said, with “at least 30%” not seeing lasting relief from drugs. Long was one of the patients for whom medication no longer worked.

So she underwent what’s considered the standard for surgical treatment of the condition: microvascular decompression, which lifts that problematic blood vessel off the nerve using a little piece of sterile Teflon.

“It’s something we do all the time, but it is brain surgery, it can take three-ish hours,” Staudt said. “The patient has to be admitted for a couple days.” Plus, there are risks that come with brain surgery, including infection and brain fluid leaks.

That said, it’s “actually curative. The pain doesn’t come back [in] about 70 to 80% of cases,” he says. For a while, this surgery helped Long. She even went off medication.

“Then just all of a sudden one day I was hit again with this intense [pain]. I mean it was worse than the first time,” she said. “It was debilitating. I knew exactly what it was.”

She tried to get it back under control with medication for months, but “it was just unbearable, even with the medicines.”

With that first surgery a bust, Long got in touch with Staudt to do a radiofrequency ablation on the nerve. The procedure uses heat to damage specific nerve fibers that carry pain signals from the face to the brain.

During the surgery, a needle is inserted about 2 cm off the side of the mouth. Using X-ray, surgeons find the trigeminal ganglion at the base of the skull, and doctors burn the nerve using radiofrequency.

“When we damage it, it stops the pain signals. You get numbness, typically,” Staudt said. “It’s like when you have novocaine for dental work.”

Unlike microvascular decompression, ablation is minimally invasive and takes just 20 to 30 minutes, with results evident as patients are “rolling out of the operating room,” Staudt said. However, the relief can be temporary. Over time, nerve fibers may recover, allowing the pain to return.

“On average, it [takes] between two to five years,” Staudt said. “I’ve seen patients 10, 20 years out. I’ve seen patients come back in a month with pain. But on average, it’s two to five years, and then they can come back and have another procedure.”

In December, Long became the first patient in the world to undergo trigeminal nerve ablation using a new system called OneRF. University Hospitals was the first health system to offer the technology.

While the technique is “nothing new,” Staudt explains, the machine allows for a novel “streamlined” procedure.

OneRF’s probe can map multiple nerve locations from a single insertion, rather than requiring surgeons to repeatedly reposition the needle.

After her treatment, Long felt immediate relief from the excruciating shocks.

“The same day I just came home and it was just like a whole bunch of numbness… Like you had got your teeth pulled,” she said. More importantly, “no shocks, no triggers, no nothing over there, nothing.”

Above all, she feels like herself again. “When I came back to work, everybody was like, Oh, you’re smiling!”

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. ناتیشا "تیش" لانگ با آنچه که به عنوان دردناک ترین احساسات شناخته شده برای انسان شناخته می شود آشنا است. از سال 2018، "درد تکان دهنده و تپنده" غیرقابل تحملی به طور تصادفی در صورت او می گذشت و هر بار از ثانیه تا چند دقیقه طول می کشید. هر ثانیه ای که می گذشت انگار یک ابدیت بود. "این فقط آنجاست و شما منتظر هستید تا آرام شود. گاهی اوقات مجبور می شدم متوقف شوم و فقط منتظر بمانم تا تمام آن شوک تمام شود تا بتوانم کار کنم."
مادر چهار فرزند مبتلا به نورالژی سه قلو است، یک بیماری عصبی که به دلیل وحشیانه بودن دوره‌های آن، به «بیماری خودکشی» ملقب شده است. لانگ گفت: «نمی‌توانی لبخند بزنی، نمی‌توانی دندان‌هایت را مسواک بزنی، نمی‌توانی صورتت را بشوی. جای تعجب نیست که این قسمت ها باعث ناراحتی عاطفی شدید، اضطراب و افسردگی می شوند. این فقط یک نام مستعار نیست - تحقیقات نشان می‌دهد افراد مبتلا به این بیماری در معرض خطر خودکشی و آسیب به خود هستند. اما متخصصان در تلاشند تا از این نام مستعار دوری کنند زیرا گزینه‌های درمانی در دسترس هستند که تسکین طولانی‌مدت را ارائه می‌کنند. پس از هفت سال طولانی، لانگ آن را با اولین روش در جهان در بیمارستان‌های دانشگاهی در اوهایو برای خودش پیدا کرد. "من از طریق درد کار می کردم ... نمی دانم چگونه این کار را انجام دادم. وقتی به گذشته نگاه می کنم، فکر می کنم چگونه این کار را کردم.

کالب ویلیامز و دریک مای به دنبال این هستند که تیم های خود را به عنوان رقبای قانونی پلی آف در برابر یکدیگر در روز پنجشنبه معرفی کنند. شیکاگو در حالی که میهن پرستان با نگرانی های فزاینده آسیب دیدگی وارد آمازون پرایم می شود، 2.5 امتیاز در میدان سرباز کسب می کند. می‌توانید هنگام ثبت‌نام در bet365 برای شرط‌بندی‌های «پنجشنبه‌شب فوتبال» یا هر بازار دیگر کتاب‌های ورزشی از کد جایزه bet365 استفاده کنید. پس از واریز واجد شرایط و شرط‌بندی 10 دلار، 200 دلار در شرط‌های جایزه دریافت خواهید کرد، چه اولین شرط شما برنده باشد یا ببازد. این بدان معناست که شما می‌توانید بدون در نظر گرفتن 20 دلار جایزه در هر یک از تیم‌ها برنده شوید و 20 دلار جایزه دریافت کنید. نتیجه کاربران جدیدی که در آریزونا، کلرادو، آیووا، ایلینویز، ایندیانا، کانزاس، کنتاکی، لوئیزیانا، مریلند، میسوری، کارولینای شمالی، نیوجرسی، اوهایو، پنسیلوانیا، تنسی، یا ویرجینیا قرار دارند می‌توانند برای این پیشنهاد ثبت‌نام کنند. می‌توانید کد جایزه bet365 را در حین ثبت‌نام وارد کنید. اما اکنون مبلغ پیشنهادی bet365 در ویرجینیا تغییری نمی‌کند. نیوانگلند سه بازیکن اصلی خط حمله را در هفته ششم از دست داد و باعث شد مای که در حال حاضر برای محافظت از فوتبال در این فصل تلاش می کند، دردسر بیشتری ایجاد کند. در همین حال، ویلیامز پس از سه بازی غیبت بدتر از این به نظر نمی رسید و 30 پاس از 36 پاس را برای 305 یارد در برابر آتلانتا انجام داد.

I’m always on the hunt for a lip balm that does more than add a little shine, and Olehenriksen’s Pout Preserve Lip Treatments have become a personal favorite.

Honestly, these are some of the most buttery-soft lip balms I’ve ever put on my lips, and I like them even better than Summer Fridays. The texture is that good: smooth, cushiony and incredibly comfortable, with a glossy finish that makes lips look instantly healthier.

The latest shade, Scandi Candy Pout Preserve Peptide Lip Treatment ($24), brings a playful pink-gummy tint to the lineup while delivering skincare-inspired benefits that go beyond a pretty pout. It combines the juicy shine I want from a lip product with a peptide-powered formula designed to hydrate, smooth and improve the appearance of lip fullness over time.

What I love about a great lip treatment is when it feels luxurious from the first swipe but also gives me a reason to keep reaching for it. Scandi Candy checks both boxes. The buttery formula glides onto lips without feeling heavy or overly sticky, leaving behind a sheer wash of pink and a high-shine finish. It’s the kind of product I can throw in my bag and reapply throughout the day, whether I’m wearing a full face of makeup or keeping things minimal.

The benefits go beyond glossy finish, though. Olehenriksen designed the treatment to help rescue dry, flaky lips, visibly smooth the lip surface and maintain hydration for up to eight hours. Peptides help support the appearance of fuller, smoother lips, while nourishing ingredients such as kokum butter and mango seed butter help condition the delicate lip area. This combination of comfort and shine is what makes a lip balm worth keeping close at all times.

The clinical results are another reason Scandi Candy stands out. In a four-week clinical study involving 39 participants, lips appeared clinically fuller in just one week. That’s a compelling selling point for anyone hoping to achieve a plumper-looking pout without relying on makeup alone. Individual results may vary, but the findings back up the treatment’s claims to visible improvements alongside everyday hydration.

Of course, the shade itself is part of the appeal. Scandi Candy has a sweet, pink-gummy look that feels playful without being over the top. I’d wear it on its own for a fresh, glossy finish or layer it over a lip liner when I want a little more definition. Either way, it gives lips that juicy, healthy-looking effect with minimal effort.

At $24, Olehenriksen’s Scandi Candy Pout Preserve Peptide Lip Treatment brings together a buttery-soft texture, lasting hydration and clinically observed improvements in lip fullness. news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. من همیشه در جستجوی یک مومیایی لب هستم که بیشتر از افزودن کمی درخشندگی داشته باشد، و درمان لب های محافظ Pout Olehenriksen به یک مورد علاقه شخصی تبدیل شده است. راستش را بخواهید، این ها برخی از کره ای ترین بالم لب هایی هستند که تا به حال روی لب هایم گذاشته ام، و من آنها را حتی بهتر از جمعه های تابستانی دوست دارم. بافت آن بسیار خوب است: صاف، نرم و فوق‌العاده راحت، با روکشی براق که لب‌ها را فوراً سالم‌تر نشان می‌دهد. جدیدترین سایه، Scandi Candy Pout Preserve Peptide Lip Treatment (24 دلار)، رنگ صورتی-لثه‌ای بازیگوش را به ترکیب می‌آورد و در عین حال فوایدی فراتر از مراقبت از پوست را ارائه می‌دهد. این درخشش آبدار من از یک محصول لب را با یک فرمول پپتیدی که برای آبرسانی، صاف کردن و بهبود ظاهر پری لب در طول زمان طراحی شده است، ترکیب می کند. چیزی که در مورد یک درمان عالی برای لب دوست دارم زمانی است که از اولین ضربه زدن احساس لوکسی به من می دهد، اما دلیلی برای ادامه یافتن به آن به من می دهد. Scandi Candy هر دو کادر را علامت می‌زند. فرمول کره ای بدون احساس سنگینی یا چسبندگی بیش از حد روی لب ها می لغزد و رنگ صورتی شفاف و درخشندگی بالایی از خود به جا می گذارد. این نوع محصولی است که می‌توانم در کیفم بیندازم و در طول روز دوباره از آن استفاده کنم، خواه آرایش کامل داشته باشم یا حداقل چیزها را حفظ کنم. اگرچه مزایای آن فراتر از سطح براق است. اولهنریکسن این درمان را برای کمک به نجات لب های خشک و پوسته پوسته، صاف کردن آشکار سطح لب و حفظ آبرسانی تا هشت ساعت طراحی کرد. پپتید

The arrest of a retired NYPD detective for the deadly road-rage shooting of a father of two on the George Washington Bridge has shocked his neighbors, who saw him as a “great person” who “cared about the community.”

Victor Romero, 62, who allegedly shot dead Koran Irvine, 46, on the traffic-packed crossing Tuesday night, had retired from New York’s Finest 25 years ago after he was shot while off duty in 2000.

The retired cop, also a married dad, lived in a quiet townhouse community in Haverstraw in Rockland County where everyone who spoke to The Post painted him as an almost perfect neighbor.

“I was so surprised when I heard this. I thought it couldn’t be true. I said, ‘No, you’re confused, it’s not him,’” Paola Ventura, 26, said of shocking news of the arrest.

“I saw him on Monday and we talked about my dog. I had a problem with my car and he helped me. One day my dog ran out of the house and he helped me get him back. I’m in shock, really,” she added.

The community board president, Ann Tartaglione, said Romero lived with his wife and his daughter who is in college and also had a son who did not live with them. She said he “wanted to help the community” and even put up his own money for a recent tree removal project.

“He cared about the community,” Tartaglione said. “I’m shocked. I really am shocked. I feel bad for the family, both families.”

Another neighbor, Luis Polanco, said Romero was “never aggressive.”

“If he could do something for you, he would do it. I got into a car accident and he helped me with the paperwork and what I needed to do. He’s so friendly. I saw him Monday afternoon,” he said in Spanish through a translator.

“I never saw him angry. He’s a great person,” added local Juan Duran.

Koran Irvine, 46, was on his way home from an overtime shift with Con-Edison when Romero allegedly fired a single shot in a fit of rage which struck him right shoulder around 7:15 p.m. on the New Jersey-bound upper level of the crossing, according to cops and his family.

Irvine was rushed to Englewood Hospital where he was later pronounced dead.

Romero admitted to being the shooter to investigators and handed the gun to police, sources told The Post.

Romero had worked with Brooklyn North Narcotics before he retired in late July of 2001 — a result of an off-duty gun battle about a year earlier at his family’s dry cleaning business, King’s Laundromat on Kings Highway in East Flatbush, police sources said.

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. دستگیری یک کارآگاه بازنشسته پلیس نیویورک به دلیل تیراندازی مرگبار به پدر دو فرزند در پل جورج واشنگتن، همسایگانش را شوکه کرده است، زیرا او را "شخصی بزرگ" می دانستند که "به جامعه اهمیت می دهد". ویکتور رومرو، 62 ساله، که گفته می شود سه شنبه شب، کوران اروین، 46 ساله را در گذرگاهی پر از ترافیک به ضرب گلوله کشت، 25 سال پیش پس از تیراندازی در حین انجام وظیفه در سال 2000، از Finest نیویورک بازنشسته شده بود. همسایه تقریباً کامل. «وقتی این را شنیدم بسیار متعجب شدم. فکر کردم نمی تواند درست باشد. پائولا ونتورا، 26 ساله، درباره خبر تکان دهنده دستگیری گفت: "نه، شما گیج شده اید، او نیست." "من او را روز دوشنبه دیدم و درباره سگم صحبت کردیم. من با ماشینم مشکل داشتم و او به من کمک کرد. یک روز سگم از خانه بیرون زد و به من کمک کرد تا او را برگردانم. من واقعاً در شوک هستم، "او افزود. رئیس هیئت انجمن، آن تارتالیونه، گفت رومرو با همسر و دخترش که در کالج است زندگی می‌کرد و همچنین پسری داشت که با آنها زندگی نمی‌کرد. او گفت که "می‌خواهد به جامعه کمک کند" و حتی پول خود را برای یک پروژه اخیر حذف درخت گذاشت. تارتالیونه گفت: "او به جامعه اهمیت می‌داد." من شوکه شده ام. واقعاً شوکه شده ام. برای خانواده، هر دو خانواده احساس بدی دارم.» همسایه دیگر، لوئیس پولانکو، گفت رومرو "هرگز تهاجمی نبود."

A quick-thinking Minnesota man jumped onto a runaway bus to rescue 19 kids after its driver suffered a “medical emergency” — and has since credited “Grey’s Anatomy” for inspiring his brave intervention.

Ebro Ahmed, 27, was having a break from his shift at the family-owned tobacco shop Ya Bricks Snacks and Tobacco in St. Paul on Monday afternoon when he saw a Battle Creek Middle School bus “roll past with the doors open” while the driver was “seizing up,” KSTP reported.

Ahmed sprang into action when the vehicle’s lights were flashing unexpectedly.

Ahmed, a business student, caught up to the bus, which was traveling at 10 mph, jumped into the driver’s seat and brought it to a halt — despite having no previous bus driving experience.

“I tried to put it in park,” he told KSTP. “I threw it in reverse by accident, and then I ended up getting it in neutral, pulled the parking brake.”

School district officials have not confirmed the driver’s condition but Ahmed told CBS he saw the driver “obviously having a medical emergency” and felt compelled to help.

“If I was just to let him drive away, I would not be human,” he said.

Remarkably, none of the 19 kids on the vehicle were injured – but Ahmed said some were a “little scared.”

“[They were] crying with their phones out getting ready to call the police,” he said.

He tried to help the driver and instructed those on board to call 911.

Ahmed has since credited the hit medical TV drama series “Grey’s Anatomy” behind his quick-thinking response.

“In ‘Grey’s Anatomy,’ you never see doctors panic,” he said.“I know it’s all acting and stuff, so I just knew to be calm and just think everything through.

“[It teaches] you about what to do in situations that you never could see yourself in,” he told ABC News.

“So it’s just something like, you know, some tips and tricks that you could use for the rest of your life.”

Ahmed’s intervention has gone viral and he has been hailed a hero by scores of commenters online.

“I really felt like it was my duty,” he told ABC News, downplaying his actions.

“Also, too, it’s kids we’re talking about, you know. Even if I were to die, it would still be worth it.”

The so-far unidentified bus driver was hospitalized following the medical emergency but has since been released.

Meanwhile some Redditors have called on the producers of Grey’s Anatomy to give Ahmed a guest role on the show as a reward for his heroism.
news.content:
پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. مردی از مینه‌سوتا که سریع فکر می‌کند، پس از اینکه راننده آن دچار "اورژانس پزشکی" شد، به اتوبوس فراری پرید تا 19 کودک را نجات دهد - و از آن زمان به دلیل الهام بخشیدن به مداخله شجاعانه‌اش، "Grey's Anatomy" را الهام گرفت. ابرو احمد، 27 ساله، در حال استراحت از شیفت خود به Bricksco Tobacco و متعلق به خانواده است. به گزارش KSTP، پل دوشنبه بعدازظهر وقتی یک اتوبوس مدرسه راهنمایی بتل کریک را دید که «با درها باز می‌گذرد» در حالی که راننده در حال «توقیف کردن» بود. احمد زمانی که چراغ‌های وسیله نقلیه به طور غیرمنتظره‌ای چشمک می‌زدند وارد عمل شد. احمد، یک دانش‌آموز بازرگانی، به اتوبوسی رسید که علی‌رغم اینکه با سرعت 10 مایل در ساعت حرکت می‌کرد – راننده قبل از آن اتوبوسی را که در حال حرکت بود پریده بود. تجربه رانندگی او به KSTP گفت: "من سعی کردم آن را در پارک قرار دهم." "به طور تصادفی آن را به عقب پرتاب کردم، و سپس آن را در حالت خنثی قرار دادم، ترمز دستی را کشیدم."
مقامات ناحیه مدرسه وضعیت راننده را تایید نکرده‌اند اما احمد به CBS گفت که راننده را دیده است که "بدیهی است که در شرایط اضطراری پزشکی قرار دارد" و احساس می‌کند که مجبور به کمک است. قابل توجه است که هیچ یک از 19 کودکی که در خودرو بودند آسیبی ندیدند - اما احمد گفت که برخی "کمی ترسیده بودند".
او گفت: «[آنها] با تلفن‌هایشان گریه می‌کردند و آماده بودند تا با پلیس تماس بگیرند.» او سعی کرد به راننده کمک کند و به سرنشینان هواپیما دستور داد تا با 911 تماس بگیرند. احمد از آن زمان به عنوان تلویزیون پزشکی موفق شناخته شد.

news.originalContent:
The US ambassador to Turkiye, Tom Barrack, says Washington’s relationship with the Middle East needs to change, from one of control to one of support.

The United States ambassador to Turkiye and special presidential envoy for Syria and Iraq says Washington’s relationship with the countries in the Middle East needs to change.

Tom Barrack says the US no longer seeks to dominate the region.

He won’t say whether the war in Iran was a mistake – but acknowledges the instability it caused has led to unintended consequences.

Barrack says President Donald Trump is against what he calls “forever wars”, and ending the US-Israel war on Iran will require a major compromise. According to him, each side will have to accept conditions it does not like.

However, he is worried that growing tensions could lead to miscalculation.

Barrack says trust is lacking between Washington and Tehran, and that is hampering talks to agree on a deal.

He tells Al Jazeera that countries in the region should not depend on the US to solve their problems and that they need to look out for themselves. He insists the Trump administration has not abandoned the region, but is rather re-examining its role.

Barrack admits that years of US involvement in the region demonstrate that intervention and regime change do not work. He says it is time to put down the guns and resolve disputes through negotiations and mutual respect.
news.content: سفیر ایالات متحده در ترکیه، تام باراک، می گوید که روابط واشنگتن با خاورمیانه باید تغییر کند، از یک رابطه کنترلی به یک رابطه حمایتی. سفیر ایالات متحده در ترکیه و نماینده ویژه رئیس جمهور در امور سوریه و عراق می گوید که روابط واشنگتن با کشورهای خاورمیانه باید تغییر کند. او نمی‌گوید که آیا جنگ در ایران اشتباه بوده است یا خیر - اما اذعان می‌کند که بی‌ثباتی ناشی از آن منجر به عواقب ناخواسته‌ای شده است. باراک می‌گوید، رئیس‌جمهور دونالد ترامپ مخالف آنچه او «جنگ‌های همیشگی» می‌خواند، است و پایان دادن به جنگ آمریکا و اسرائیل علیه ایران مستلزم یک سازش بزرگ است. به گفته وی، هر طرف باید شرایطی را بپذیرد که دوست ندارد. باراک می گوید که اعتماد بین واشنگتن و تهران کم است و این امر مذاکرات برای توافق بر سر یک توافق را مختل می کند. او به الجزیره می گوید که کشورهای منطقه نباید برای حل مشکلات خود به آمریکا وابسته باشند و باید مراقب خود باشند. او اصرار دارد که دولت ترامپ منطقه را رها نکرده است، بلکه در حال بررسی مجدد نقش آن است. باراک اعتراف می کند که سال ها دخالت ایالات متحده در منطقه نشان می دهد که مداخله و تغییر رژیم کارساز نیست. او می گوید زمان آن فرا رسیده است که اسلحه ها را زمین بگذاریم و اختلافات را از طریق مذاکره و احترام متقابل حل کنیم.

news.originalContent:
Firebrand student leader has become the face of the youth protest movement taking on Modi’s Hindu majoritarian government.

New Delhi, India – As India’s leader of the opposition, Rahul Gandhi, marched with tens of thousands of supporters to the country’s Supreme Court on October 12 to submit a petition seeking the sacking of the nation’s election chief, he rested his hands on the shoulders of two women ahead.

One was his 54-year-old younger sister Priyanka, whom Rahul – two years older – has described as his “best friend” and most trusted lieutenant. The other was a 29-year-old student leader who few knew outside college politics until these past few months: Neha Bora.

After 12 years in power, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has recently faced a number of his toughest political challenges, as a Gen Z-led movement first forced him to dump his education minister after a series of examination scandals and is now pressuring him over controversial changes to India’s electoral rolls that have stripped 130 million people of the right to vote.

Yet while the satirical Cockroach group that drove mass protests at Jantar Mantar in the heart of the capital New Delhi over the last few months has grabbed more global headlines, Bora, from a left student group, has rapidly emerged as one of the most defiant faces of a generation that is challenging Modi’s grip on power.

Bora is slight of build, with dark hair, and speaks in a deep, resonant voice. But where Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders have sat in for protests, held placards, and quickly been picked up by police, Bora has made almost a game out of tricking security forces out to get protesters – using street politics tactics that have turned the student into a cult figure among sections of the country’s youth unhappy with Modi’s policies and appointees.

Software developers have turned Bora into video-game characters, leaping over barricades, collecting “democracy” points and dodging police in Mario-style games. Social media users edit and share Bora’s quick-paced fan edits, confronting police personnel, shared by tens of thousands and viewed by millions. And veteran opposition leaders like Gandhi lean on the student leader – literally – in tense situations.

“Can we please, please call Neha the Goddess of Democracy,” asked Nishita Nath, a 24-year-old student in the capital, sitting under a tree in central Delhi earlier this month. The reference was to Hong Kong protest leader Agnes Chow, who earned that epithet as she campaigned against laws that critics have called draconian, imposed by Beijing on the Chinese territory.

Such comparisons, though, are the last thing Bora wants – as a leader of a protest movement seeking to cut a political demigod down to size.

Bora has spent nearly a decade studying the arts at universities in Delhi, including as a postdoctoral theatre student at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), a premier public university that has been a cauldron of political activism for decades.

There, Bora joined the left student organisation, All India Students’ Association (AISA), which has been a major force at JNU for more than three decades.

Now the national president of AISA, Bora and comrades joined the Cockroach activists earlier this year in camping for weeks at Jantar Mantar seeking the resignation of the education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan.

But it was earlier this month that Bora moved from the sidelines to centre stage in the national consciousness.

On October 10, the Modi government locked down the heart of the capital New Delhi as thousands of young people prepared to protest, demanding the election chief’s resignation.

Police moved swiftly to detain protesters arriving by train and buses, confined student leaders to their homes, and even boarded a plane to detain top leaders of the Cockroach movement moments after the plane landed in the capital.

But Bora disappeared into the shadows, remaining beyond the police’s reach.

Then, that afternoon, Bora appeared live on Instagram, wearing a One Piece T-shirt – a symbol adopted by global Gen Z protest movements – and leading a crowd of a few hundred through affluent South Delhi, kilometres from the police barricades.

In half an hour, the police chased down Bora, who was dragged away in a police van and released many hours later.

To understand Bora’s street politics, one needs to turn a few pages back. The AISA was founded in August 1990 as the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation, a party that emerged from a Maoist-led communist rebellion that began in eastern India in 1967, inspired by a peasant uprising in the village of Naxalbari, West Bengal. The Maoists were called Naxals, after the village.

The party operated clandestinely in the face of state crackdown for at least three decades before rejecting armed violence – a number of its splinters, however, still seek a violent overthrow of the Indian state – and embracing parliamentary democracy in the 1990s.

But the party has changed, although it retains some of its legacy DNA. On October 10, AISA knew that the police would preemptively come after youth leaders. So its activists hid Bora.

“We have been an underground party before, before our party contested elections; so, we followed the same tactics, some kind of guerrilla [tactics],” said Danish Ali, a 25-year-old AISA student leader and a friend of Bora.

Ali said the party relies on tactics that “revolutionaries like Bhagat Singh” – an anti-colonial activist who was executed by British authorities in 1931, aged 23 – “used in resisting colonial rule.”

While Bhagat Singh, a self-described socialist in his time, remains a hero worshipped across political strains, Modi’s Hindu majoritarian Bharatiya Janata Party has demonised left politics. In parliament and state legislatures, too, left parties have in recent years suffered historic setbacks.

After protests won the resignation of Education Minister Pradhan, the prime minister cautioned in his Independence Day Speech in August against “urban naxals” or “intellectual naxals” – references that Modi’s party have used to describe opponents and critics of all political stripes.

There’s a reason, argues Bora, that Modi’s party is so scared of the left.

“How do you claim to be the champions of nationalism if you do not delegitimise the people who are actual inheritors of the radical legacy that got India independence?” Bora said, speaking to Al Jazeera.

Bora was born in Khatima, a small town in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand. The family then lived in Jammu, Bengaluru, Amritsar, and Lucknow as her father’s service in the Indian Army frequently took them from one posting to another.

As a teenager, differences in political opinions with the family grew, to a point where Bora was “cut off”. Then, a few months ago, Bora staged a 23-day hunger strike in solidarity with the students at the Jantar Mantar protest strip.

Bora recalled being surprised when someone among the thousands-strong crowd said: “A woman is there, saying she is your mother; shall I let her in?” A motherly leg massage followed.

That hunger strike also helped establish her on a national level, where people could finally engage with her left politics, said N Sai Balaji, a senior AISA leader, who advises Bora closely.

“India’s aspirational class, who felt betrayed by the government’s broken promises, found hope in people like Neha who were sitting selflessly. That’s where the whole propaganda vanishes. Suddenly, the so-called ‘anti-nationals’ become humans too,” Balaji told Al Jazeera, referring to a term often used by Modi government supporters for critics.

The cameras on Bora are new, but the activism and talent for political mobilisation are not.

In 2019, protests against proposed amendments to India’s citizenship laws, which were seen as discriminatory against Muslims, were a true political awakening, Bora told Al Jazeera.

That kickstarted Bora’s participation and eventual leadership of students-led movements. At JNU, Bora “distributed pamphlets and mobilised students for years, canvassing students’ votes for AISA, going to room to room”, Ali said.

Bora lives and breathes politics, “speaking out for Muslim political prisoners”, for instance, he added, referring to youth leaders like Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam, who have now been in jail for more than six years without a trial. Bora, he said, is “bravely honest”.

The October 10 episode, when Bora evaded the police, was no one-off. Multiple smaller coups followed that week, as Bora outmanoeuvred government forces to stage demonstrations with supporters in parts of central Delhi.

Then Bora’s photos and videos would flood social media by evening: Straining against the officers’ grip, yet smiling for the cameras, flashing a victory sign, fighting to break free, often hoisted in the air by policewomen.

Bora listens to ghazals by Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, the celebrated Pakistani vocalist who brought Sufi music to a global audience.

But the young left leader is a good singer too, say friends, and plays the tambourine.

And unlike many others from that political ideology in previous generations who have been criticised for being too dogmatic and theoretical in their use of Marxism, Bora is the new generation student, Balaji points out, “who grew up on the internet and knows that language [to engage with youth] very well”.

Still, despite Bora’s growing political stature, any left student leader faces a string of formidable challenges to leave a mark in Indian politics, analysts say.

First, AISA’s influence is concentrated in university campuses and pockets of student activism in northern India. Its parent party, the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation, is also a small force in national politics.

The party has two members in parliament, both from the eastern state of Bihar, and has never governed a state on its own.

“AISA does not have a formidable bridge for its student leaders to transition from campus to constituencies,” said Asim Ali, a political analyst based in New Delhi.

In Indian electoral politics, a politician needs a geographical stronghold, Ali argued, where they have a reliable block of voters on the ground. “Bora does not have that kind of blocks or a base,” he added.

One way into electoral politics for leaders like Bora is to transition into a mainstream political party with wider presence in India – such as Gandhi’s Congress party – like many left leaders have done. But there, different challenges exist. “Mere popular appeal doesn’t float you through entrenched hold of existing leaders in big parties like the Congress,” said the analyst.

Nonetheless, whether Bora stays with her left-aligned party or moves closer to groups like the Congress, “Neha appears to be rising above nuances of political cleavages – and building a real block of young voters behind her, even if it is not a textbook voter bank in the Indian context,” Ali, the analyst, said.

Among them is Nath, the Delhi University student who isn’t a member of AISA but is a staunch Bora supporter. She often ends up chasing the student leader on streets amid protests. Last week, Nath spent hours every morning running in her neighbourhood “to practice and keep up with Neha”.

“The way Neha speaks: The pauses, the tune in her voice, the flying hair. All I see on my Instagram is Neha,” Nath said. “My last week’s high point was when I held Neha’s hand while she was running in the chaos.”

That chaos likely isn’t going anywhere, with the Modi government facing pressure from the mainstream opposition, the Cockroach movement, and student groups.

Nor is Bora, says Ali, the political analyst.

Bora “is tapping a newfound place in Indian politics”, he said. “Neha is not a moment, for sure, but is here to stay.”

news.originalContent:
The ongoing mystery around Mat Barzal’s return date may serve to obscure a more interesting question: How will he fit with the Islanders upon his return?

There’s no doubt the Islanders could use Barzal in their lineup as soon as possible. Other than Matthew Schaefer, he’s the only truly dynamic skater they have — the only other guy who can turn a nothing shift into something at the snap of a finger. The Islanders have played well on the back of their defense through a 5-3-1 start and received good secondary scoring, but Barzal helps address the most glaring hole they have — and one that, as the season wears on, will become much tougher to hide.

Still, there are two levels on which Barzal’s eventual return will necessitate an adjustment on his part.

The first is injury-related: Whenever Barzal does return, he’ll be launching into the middle of a season without any training camp or games, competing against players who have had plenty of both.
news.content: رمز و راز ادامه دار در مورد تاریخ بازگشت مت بارزال ممکن است یک سوال جالب تر را پنهان کند: او چگونه با جزیره نشینان پس از بازگشت هماهنگ می شود؟ شکی نیست که جزیره نشینان می توانند در اسرع وقت از بارزال در ترکیب خود استفاده کنند. به غیر از متیو شفر، او تنها اسکیت باز واقعاً پویا است - تنها مرد دیگری که می تواند تغییر هیچ چیز را با یک انگشت به چیزی تبدیل کند. جزیره‌ای‌ها با شروع 5-3-1 در پشت خط دفاعی خود خوب بازی کرده‌اند و گل‌های ثانویه خوبی دریافت کرده‌اند، اما بارزال کمک می‌کند تا به خیره‌ترین حفره‌ای که دارند رسیدگی شود – و با گذشت فصل، پنهان کردن آن بسیار سخت‌تر خواهد شد. اولین مورد مربوط به مصدومیت است: هر زمان که بارزال بازگردد، او در میانه یک فصل بدون هیچ کمپ تمرینی یا بازی شروع می شود و با بازیکنانی رقابت می کند که هر دو را به وفور داشته اند.

news.originalContent:
El-Sayed and Rogers also tackle immigration in Michigan while Kansas candidates spar over Ukraine.

El-Sayed in face-off against rival Rogers for Michigan Senate seat

Candidates in two key United States Senate races have faced off in their final debates, less than two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections.

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers exchanged accusations on Wednesday regarding their political views and the US-Israel war on Iran.

In Kansas, Republican Senator Roger Marshall and his Democratic opponent, Adam Hamilton, disagreed about the rising price of diesel and President Donald Trump’s plan to import Russian fuel.

The results of both elections will influence which party ends up in control of the Senate. The Republicans currently dominate Congress’s upper chamber with 53 of its 100 seats. Democrats hold 45, and two senators are independents who caucus with the Democratic Party.

Here are some of the key takeaways from these debates:

Rogers questioned some of Trump’s tariffs, describing them as a “mixed bag”. While he supported taking steps to bring automobile manufacturing back to Michigan from China and Mexico, he questioned the impact of tariffs on Canada.

“I have stepped back and said maybe these Canadian tariffs were not well thought through,” Rogers said, referring to the close ties between the automobile industries of the two countries.

Michigan sits on the Canadian border and is the US state with the most car-manufacturing jobs.

Rogers insisted he would put Michigan’s interests first if elected.

“If it’s good for Michigan, I’m going to be for it. If it’s bad for Michigan, I’m going to be against it,” he said.

He pushed back against El-Sayed’s repeated references to Trump.

“The bingo game ought to be how many times can he put the word Trump in any answer that he has given in the last, whatever, 30 minutes,” he said. “It’s ridiculous.”

El-Sayed accused Rogers of supporting the war on Iran, which he blamed for rising fuel and food prices in the US.

He said he believed Iran had posed a threat to US national security but argued that the 2015 nuclear deal, negotiated under former President Barack Obama, had helped to contain it through diplomacy.

The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) was signed by Iran and several world powers, including the US. It placed restrictions on Iran’s nuclear programme, including strictly limiting uranium enrichment and compelling Iran to submit to international inspections, in exchange for sanctions relief.

Trump withdrew the US from the agreement in 2018, arguing that it failed to adequately address Iran’s nuclear ambitions and ballistic missile programme and support for armed groups in the region.

El-Sayed criticised Trump for abandoning the agreement during his first term and launching a war against Iran during his second.

El-Sayed argued that Americans have been left paying the price.

“The consequences of this war are that you are paying nearly $5 [per gallon, or 3.8 litres] in gas. You’re paying more in groceries because of the price of diesel,” he said.

According to the American Automobile Association (AAA), regular petrol in Michigan averaged $4.44 per gallon on Wednesday, up from $2.92 a year earlier. Diesel prices rose from $3.62 to $6.41 per gallon over the same period.

El-Sayed also sought to tie Rogers to Trump, who is expected to campaign in Michigan on Sunday.

“Donald Trump is on the ballot through Mike Rogers. They are hip-to-hip on this war, and you are paying the cost,” he said.

“Mike Rogers has been promoting this war since before he was in Congress. He’s got a war for everything, and he won’t back off the war now.”

Rogers appealed to Democrats who supported Haley Stevens, whom El-Sayed defeated in the Democratic primary.

“If you were a Haley Stevens voter and you came out of this and you said, ‘Man, I just can’t do it. He’s too extreme,’ well, guess what? You’ll have a home with us,” he said, and claimed that a growing number of Democrats are now backing his campaign.

One of the more contentious moments of the debate came when Rogers suggested El-Sayed had the same supporters as groups like Hamas, allegations El-Sayed pushed back against.

“You can grin and you can smile and you can talk real pretty, but I’m going to tell you what, that is a risk to our national security,” Rogers said. He told reporters after the debate that he questions whether El-Sayed could get a security clearance for senators if he’s elected.

El-Sayed called the allegations “shameful”.

Immigration sparked another heated exchange.

Rogers defended the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown, arguing that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations had helped reduce crime.

“We should continue to do that. Find those folks who are committing crimes and get them the heck out of the country,” Rogers said.

El-Sayed criticised ICE’s tactics, accusing Rogers of supporting raids on schools, workplaces and places of worship.

“He supports ICE running through your streets. They don’t have to tell you who they are. They don’t have to tell you why they’re there,” El-Sayed said.

“I believe that we don’t need ICE,” he added.

Marshall said Russia’s war on Ukraine rather than the Iran war was responsible for soaring diesel prices during his final debate with his Democratic challenger.

The Republican’s comments echoed Trump’s recent criticism of Ukraine, including his claim that Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have caused rising fuel costs.

Trump has agreed a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release stocks of Russian diesel to the US and global markets to ease prices, an idea Marshall greeted with some reservations.

“It doesn’t sound like a great idea,” Marshall said. But he added: “If this brings Russia to the bargaining table and it ends the war, then I am all for it right now.”

Hamilton responded angrily: “What you said just now is you’re going to sell out our friends in Ukraine. That’s not OK.”

Diesel prices have become a key campaign issue in Kansas, where farmers depend heavily on the fuel. According to AAA, diesel averaged $6.32 a gallon this week in the state, compared with $3.62 a year earlier.

Hamilton blamed the price rises on Trump’s war on Iran and called for a temporary suspension of federal fuel taxes. Marshall has also said he wants the war to end soon but has not committed to trying to force Trump to end it.

Hamilton criticised recent ICE raids while Marshall defended Trump’s border policies.

Both candidates expressed cautious support for making E-Verify, a system that allows employers to check whether workers are legally authorised to work in the US, mandatory for businesses.

“I think it’s a good idea. Of course, the devil’s in the details,” Marshall said, arguing that Republicans had secured the border and could now focus on fixing the immigration system.

Hamilton challenged Marshall, who had mentioned delivering babies for undocumented parents during his medical career.

“Did you also call ICE and ask them to be taken away? What did you do with these people?” Hamilton asked.

“You had compassion for them in delivering these children, but then you support quotas. They’re going to have people taken away. Hutchinson, Kansas, I was there. There was a preschool teacher arrested in front of her children,” he added.

Hamilton also criticised recent ICE raids in southwestern Kansas, warning that they were frightening workers and disrupting the agricultural industry.

“People are terrified when ICE shows up because they’ve been militarised, politicised, and so people don’t show up at work,” he said.

“We don’t want people terrified in our communities.”

Hamilton criticised the use of US weapons in Gaza while Marshall defended Washington’s alliance with Israel.

Hamilton said he supported providing Israel with defensive weapons but opposed supplying bombs used in attacks on densely populated areas.

“When you see entire cities flattened in Gaza, now we’re not just talking about rooting out Hamas,” Hamilton said.

“They’re using our aid to buy our weapons and then dropping them on innocent civilians. That’s just not OK. It’s not decent. It’s not who we are as Americans.”

Marshall defended Israel as one of Washington’s closest allies and was asked whether there were circumstances in which he would block a weapons sale.

“I’m sure there is. I’m not sure what it would be,” Marshall said.

Marshall stressed the importance of strong military alliances but said Washington should prioritise domestic concerns.

“I want to make sure that our borders are secure. Let’s take care of things at home first,” he said.

السید و راجرز همچنین به مهاجرت در میشیگان می پردازند در حالی که نامزدهای کانزاس بر سر اوکراین می جنگند. السید در رویارویی با رقیب راجرز برای کرسی سنای میشیگان
نامزدهای دو رقابت کلیدی سنای ایالات متحده در مناظره های نهایی خود، کمتر از دو هفته مانده به انتخابات میان دوره ای 3 نوامبر، با هم روبرو شده اند. در میشیگان، عبدالالسید دموکرات و مایک راجرز جمهوری‌خواه روز چهارشنبه در مورد دیدگاه‌های سیاسی خود و جنگ آمریکا و اسرائیل علیه ایران اتهاماتی را رد و بدل کردند. در کانزاس، سناتور جمهوری‌خواه راجر مارشال و رقیب دموکرات‌اش، آدام همیلتون، در مورد افزایش قیمت گازوئیل و طرح دونالد ترامپ رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا برای پایان دادن به تاثیرات حزبی در واردات نفت روسیه، اختلاف نظر داشتند. سنا جمهوری خواهان در حال حاضر با 53 کرسی از 100 کرسی بر مجلس فوقانی کنگره تسلط دارند. دموکرات ها دارای 45 نفر هستند و دو سناتور مستقل هستند که با حزب دموکرات همکاری می کنند. در اینجا برخی از نکات کلیدی این بحث ها آورده شده است:
راجرز برخی از تعرفه های ترامپ را زیر سوال برد و آنها را "کیسه ای ترکیبی" توصیف کرد. در حالی که او از برداشتن گام‌هایی برای بازگرداندن خودروسازی از چین و مکزیک به میشیگان حمایت می‌کند، اما تأثیر تعرفه‌ها بر کانادا را زیر سوال می‌برد. راجرز با اشاره به روابط نزدیک بین صنایع خودروسازی دو کشور گفت: «من عقب‌نشینی کرده‌ام و گفتم شاید این تعرفه‌های کانادا به خوبی فکر نشده باشد.»

news.originalContent:
Civilian with a disability shot dead by Israeli forces during raid in Jamla, in western Deraa countryside, SANA reports.

Israeli forces have killed a man with a disability during a raid in Syria’s southern Deraa governorate, Syria’s state news agency SANA reported.

The civilian was shot dead early on Thursday in the village of Jamla in Daraa’s western countryside, where Israeli forces had deployed snipers on rooftops, SANA reported.

The victim’s body was brought to Deraa National Hospital, the agency added.

The Israeli military did not immediately comment on the report.

Since Syria’s longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad was removed in December 2024, the Israeli army has waged hundreds of strikes in the country and routinely moved forces into Syrian territory.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has condemned Israel’s “aggressions”, saying they “undermine peace and security”.

In recent days, Israeli forces have reportedly carried out raids and destroyed olive groves in Quneitra province, near Deraa.

In one raid on Thursday, in the village of Turnejeh in the Quneitra countryside, Israeli forces searched homes and detained one person, according to SANA.

Earlier in the week, Israeli forces destroyed trees in a large field by the village of Saida, the agency reported.

Syria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday condemned “the intensification of incursions by the Israeli occupation” in Quneitra and Deraa.

Israeli officials have repeatedly said they plan to keep troops in what they call a “security zone” in southern Syria.

The two countries have opened negotiations for a security agreement, but the talks have been largely stalled since the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran in February.
news.content: به گزارش سانا، یک غیرنظامی معلول در جریان حمله به جمله، در حومه غربی درعا، توسط نیروهای اسرائیلی به ضرب گلوله کشته شد. خبرگزاری دولتی سوریه، سانا گزارش داد، نیروهای اسرائیلی یک مرد معلول را در جریان یورش به استان درعا در جنوب سوریه کشتند. این غیرنظامی اوایل روز پنجشنبه در روستای جمله در حومه درعا در حومه درعا به ضرب گلوله کشته شد. سانا گزارش داد که پشت بام ها. این آژانس افزود: جسد قربانی به بیمارستان ملی درعا منتقل شد. ارتش اسرائیل بلافاصله در مورد این گزارش اظهار نظر نکرد. از زمانی که بشار اسد حاکم دیرینه سوریه در دسامبر 2024 برکنار شد، ارتش اسرائیل صدها حمله در این کشور انجام داده و به طور معمول نیروها را به داخل خاک سوریه منتقل کرده است. "صلح و امنیت را تضعیف می کند". بنا بر گزارش سانا، نیروهای اسرائیلی در روزهای اخیر حملاتی را انجام داده و باغ‌های زیتون را در استان قنیطره در نزدیکی درعا منهدم کرده‌اند. به گزارش سانا، در یک حمله روز پنجشنبه، در روستای تورنجه در حومه قنیطره، نیروهای اسرائیلی خانه‌ها را تفتیش کردند و یک نفر را بازداشت کردند. اوایل هفته، نیروهای اسرائیلی گزارش داده بود که درختان مزرعه‌ای بزرگ در یک روستای صعدا را تخریب کردند. وزارت امور خارجه سوریه روز یکشنبه «تشدید تهاجمات اشغالگران اسرائیل» به قنیطره و درعا را محکوم کرد. مقامات اسرائیلی بارها گفته‌اند که قصد دارند نیروهای خود را در این منطقه نگه دارند.

news.originalContent:
Across Europe, an autumn of anger is taking hold.

In France, student protests over overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages have grown into a broader public outcry.

In recent weeks, separate protests have also erupted in Belgium, Italy, Portugal, Spain and Albania.

The grievances differ, from unaffordable housing and low wages to rising fuel costs, education and political accountability.

But the frustration is increasingly shared: paying more, getting less, and struggling to afford a decent life, even with a job.

Governments face demands for relief while wrestling with high debt, rising borrowing costs and, in several countries, looming elections.
news.content: در سرتاسر اروپا، پاییز خشم در راه است. در فرانسه، اعتراضات دانش‌آموزان به دلیل شلوغی کلاس‌ها و کمبود معلم به یک اعتراض عمومی گسترده‌تر تبدیل شده است. در هفته‌های اخیر، اعتراض‌های جداگانه‌ای در بلژیک، ایتالیا، پرتغال، اسپانیا و آلبانی نیز به راه افتاده است. نارضایتی‌ها متفاوت است، از مسکن غیرقابل مقرون‌به‌صرفه و دستمزدهای پایین، هزینه‌های تحصیلی و هزینه‌های سنگین سیاسی. اما این ناامیدی به طور فزاینده ای مشترک است: پرداخت بیشتر، دریافت کمتر، و تلاش برای تامین یک زندگی مناسب، حتی با داشتن شغل.

Brazil’s president appeals to undecided voters ahead of run-off

Brazil’s two presidential candidates Lula and Bolsonaro are trying to win over the 30 million voters who abstained in the first round of voting as they near Sunday’s crucial run-off. Al Jazeera’s Lucia Newman was at a rally by President Lula in the key swing state of Minas Gerais.

news.title: «ورشکسته و غرق در بدهی»؛ آخرین سلطان امپراتوری عثمانی چگونه درگذشت؟
news.originalSummary:
منبع تصویر، Universal Images Group via Getty Images

محمد ششم، سلطان وحیدالدین، آخرین سلطان امپراتوری عثمانی، گفته بود: «من بر بالش نرم تخت سلطنت ننشستم، بر خاکسترهای آتش نشستم.»

او پس از مرگ برادرش محمد پنجم رشاد، در سال ۱۹۱۸ به سلطنت رسید.
